questions.q: To keep the top 2 customers by spend within each region, which SQL construct is the standard approach?
options: ORDER BY total LIMIT 2 with no partition
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY region ORDER BY total DESC), then filter rn <= 2
GROUP BY region HAVING COUNT(*) = 2
SELECT DISTINCT region
questions.explain: A window function numbered within each region lets you keep the first N rows per group.

questions.q: In the cohort retention query, why is a LEFT JOIN used?
options: To keep customers who did not return, so they count in the denominator
It is faster than any other join
To remove customers with no orders
To sort the results
questions.explain: An inner join would drop non-returning customers and inflate the retention rate.

questions.q: The last cohort shows 0.00 retention because the data ends before its next month. What should you do?
options: Report it as a 0% retention rate
Delete the cohort silently
Flag that its window is incomplete and exclude or footnote it
Fill it with the average of other cohorts
questions.explain: The next month has not been observed, so the zero reflects missing time, not customer behavior.

questions.q: How do you deduplicate rows by email in pandas, keeping the most recent record?
options: df.dropna('email')
df.groupby('email').sum()
df.merge(df, on='email')
Sort by updated_at, then drop_duplicates('email', keep='last')
questions.explain: After sorting ascending by update time, keep='last' retains the newest row per email.

questions.q: Which habit most helps in a live SQL interview?
options: Writing the whole query silently before speaking
Restating the question, asking about ties and NULLs, and narrating as you build
Memorizing exact queries
Avoiding test data
questions.explain: Interviewers evaluate reasoning; clarifying and narrating shows it and catches mistakes early.
